parts.original_hypothesis: The output is the sigmoid of an additive logit: the eight parts (seven ReLU parts and the direct linear terms) each add a weighted exit value, and the parts combine by addition at the output (function preservation of the refactored model: max error 8.9e-16). On the training split the model has AUC 0.882 and accuracy 0.810; replacing each nonlinear unit by its affine fit leaves AUC 0.860 (a nonlinear gain of 0.022), so the model is largely a weighted sum of line features with a few gates and caps. Main effects: x's open twos raise x's predicted chance (directly and through the x-open-twos cap, which saturates near two open twos: whole-model chance 44%, 92% and 97% at 0, 2 and 6 open twos at the typical case); x's open singles raise it (chance 13% at 0 to 81% at 10, through the x-lines-vs-o-centre pair, the x-singles-vs-twos gate and the o-centre-x-singles gate); o's open singles and open twos lower it (chance 88% to 8% as o's open twos go from 0 to 6, through the o-lines ramp, the quiet-o gate and the pair). Gates: a single o threat switches the o-lines ramp and the x-open-twos cap off and drops the chance to 37% from 74% at the typical case; the centre column block raises the chance when x holds the centre and lowers it when the centre column is crowded by either side (heavy-centre gate). The largest parts by AUC loss when switched off are the o-lines ramp (0.8414), the x-open-twos cap (0.8328) and the direct terms (0.8457), against 0.8815 with everything on. x's threats coincide with x's open threes on the training rows (0 rows differ) and o's threats with o's open threes (0 rows differ); both are rare (660 and 765 positions), and the parity splits of threats are rarer still (66 positions with an x odd-row threat, 100 with an o odd-row threat), so their weights are fitted to few rows and are described, not explained. The sixteen inputs are each connected and enter through split copies, one per part.

parts.original_hypothesis: A ReLU gate that switches on when o holds the centre column while x has many open singles and few centre pieces, and when on raises x's predicted chance. It is on for 9018 of the 54045 training positions (16.7%), where x wins at a rate of 70.9% against 64.8% on the rest; its value when on is small, so its whole-model effect is small: switching it off changes the training AUC from 0.8815 to 0.8796, and the part raises the mean predicted chance by 0.011. Self-probe: with o holding two centre pieces and x's centre count at 0 at the typical case, the gate turns on as x's open singles rise (off at three singles, value 0.03 at four and 0.90 at ten) while the whole-model chance rises from 17% to 93%; sweeping o's centre pieces at the typical case the gate is off at 0 and 1 centre piece and on from 2 (value 0.75, rising to 2.48 at 4). The gate is also on for 1426 positions in which o's centre count is 0 (x's open singles alone can switch it). Reading: 'o's centre pieces + x's open singles - x's centre pieces' predicts the gate being on with AUC 0.82 (score 0.65, partial); the reading holds for part of its behaviour.
